ambiguities: The narrator's aside that if Forcheville had read a letter addressed to Swann he would have seen 'des mots autrement tendres' faintly implies Swann is more tenderly regarded by Odette than Forcheville, but the comparison is hypothetical, filtered through Swann's own jealous perspective, and too unstable to score as a distinct appraisal event for either candidate.

Forcheville's concealed presence and hasty departure are already the evidentiary basis of the accepted E1 (Odette's deception); the passage gives him no distinct local outcome beyond that already-captured movement, so he was not separately scored.

Odette detaining Swann by the arm and expressing regret at having missed his visit could be read as a gesture of favor toward Swann, but the narrator immediately frames it as a missed clue within her ongoing deception, leaving the sincerity (and thus any status effect on Swann) too uncertain to score.
